newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.

text.p: Swiss shares closed slightly higher, but near the day's lows, following a bout of profit-taking late in the day triggered by Wall Street's weak start, dealers said.

Early rises in a few blue chips, such as Roche, Novartis and Nestle, had set the stage for a generally good session, dealers said. Trading volumes were relatively high, but investors were mostly cautious, they added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 1.8 points, or 0.04 percent, higher at 4,127.3 and the broad Swiss Performance Index advanced 2.90 points, or 0.11 percent, to 2,642.45.
Novartis registered shares led the actives list, adding four francs to 1,586. The company is due to release its 1996 sales figures on Tuesday before the bourse opening.
Roche certificates advanced 10 francs to 11,790 after a day's high of 11,930. Clariant gave up 17 francs, or 2.46 percent, to finish at 675.
ABB slid 18 francs, or 1.03 percent, to 1,727 after temporarily reaching 1,756. Sulzer fell seven francs to 937 while Alusuisse gained 10 francs to end at 1,146.
Among financials, insurers Winterthur and Swiss Re stood out with an advance of five francs to 938 and 22 francs to 1,391, respectively.
Speculative buying, a buy recommendation and positive research studies were said to be the reasons behind the Winterthur advance.
Among the banks, UBS bearer shares lost six francs to end at 1,174 after a volatile day.
Credit Suisse Group was up 0.25 francs to 141.50 while SBC gave up 0.75 francs to close at 249.
